title: Chorionic villus sampling (CVS)
what: Guided by ultrasound, the doctor takes a tiny piece of tissue from the developing placenta. It is tested for your baby's chromosomes and genes.
why: When the first screening shows a high risk or there is an inherited condition in the family. Usually at 11 to 14 weeks.
duration: the procedure itself usually takes 15 to 30 minutes; first results usually come in a few days, full results in up to 2 weeks
tell_doctor: Your blood type and Rh factor
Infections such as hepatitis or HIV

prepare.title: Your decision
prepare.text: A genetics doctor will explain beforehand why it is done, the risks, and what the test shows. You sign a consent form.

prepare.title: Method
prepare.text: Usually the needle goes through your belly. Sometimes a thin tube goes through the cervix. Your doctor will say which suits you.

prepare.title: Bladder
prepare.text: Sometimes you are asked to come with a full bladder, sometimes the opposite. Check with the clinic.

steps: You lie on your back, and the doctor does an ultrasound
The skin on your belly is cleaned and numbed
Guided by ultrasound, a thin needle is passed to the developing placenta
A tiny piece of tissue is taken. It takes a few seconds
The needle is removed, and your baby's heartbeat is checked
feel: A prick and pressure or cramping in your belly
Afterward, period-like cramps for a few hours
after: You usually rest at the clinic for 20 to 30 minutes
For 1 to 2 days, take it easy: no lifting, exercise, or sex
If you are Rh negative, you usually get an anti-D injection
A genetics doctor will explain the results
red_flags: Bleeding like a period, or severe pain: call emergency services
Fluid leaking from the vagina: see a doctor urgently
A fever over 38°C (100.4°F) or chills: see a doctor urgently

faq.q: How is this different from amniocentesis?
faq.a: It is done earlier, at 11 to 14 weeks, and takes placenta tissue instead of fluid. You also get the answer sooner.

faq.q: Is there a risk to the pregnancy?
faq.a: There is a small risk of miscarriage. Your doctor will explain it for your situation.

faq.q: Do I have to have it?
faq.a: No. It is your choice. Your doctor will help you weigh the benefits and risks.

reminders.text: CVS tomorrow. Check whether you need a full bladder. Ask someone to take you home.
